lobby.tagline: An AI that listens to your meeting and quietly researches what you talk about — prior art, unfamiliar terms, evidence and counterpoints — on a shared canvas, so nobody has to stop the conversation to look things up.
lobby.mockBanner: Demo mode: no API keys are configured. Try the scripted bilingual meeting below, or add keys to .env for live research.
lobby.serverUnreachable: Cannot reach the server. Is it running?
lobby.title: Meeting title
lobby.demoText: Replays a short Japanese/English meeting so you can watch the agent find prior art, explain terms, check claims and challenge a quick consensus.
lobby.demoTitle: Demo: building a meeting transcription tool

captureModeHint.roomMicrophone: One laptop in the room records everyone; voices are separated automatically.
captureModeHint.onlineHostCapture: One person shares the meeting tab (or system audio) plus their own microphone. No setup for others.
captureModeHint.onlinePerParticipant: Each participant opens this room and streams their own microphone. Best speaker names; needs headphones.
captureModeHint.zoomRtms: Zoom sends each participant's audio to the server. Requires a Zoom RTMS app (see docs).
captureModeHint.demo: No microphone: a scripted meeting is replayed.
captureModeHint.meetingBot: A bot joins the Google Meet / Teams / Zoom meeting and sends each participant's voice with their name. The host must admit the bot.

captureHelp.roomMicrophone: Place the laptop in the middle of the table. Browser noise suppression is turned off so distant voices are kept.
captureHelp.onlinePerParticipant: Your microphone is sent as your own voice. Use headphones so others' voices from your speakers are not recorded twice.
captureHelp.demo: The scripted meeting provides the audio.

onlineHostCapture.inPerson: Share the meeting audio and your microphone.
onlineHostCapture.zoom:
Zoom web client: choose the Zoom tab and tick “Share tab audio”.
Zoom desktop on Windows: choose “Entire screen” and tick “Share system audio”.
Your microphone is sent as a separate, named stream.
onlineHostCapture.googleMeet: Use Google Meet in a regular Chrome or Edge tab. Choose that Meet tab and tick “Also share tab audio”. Your own microphone is sent as a separate, named stream.
onlineHostCapture.teams: Teams web: choose the Teams tab and tick “Share tab audio”. Teams desktop on Windows: choose “Entire screen” and tick “Share system audio”.
onlineHostCapture.other: Choose the meeting tab (or entire screen) and enable audio sharing.

captureHelp.meetingBot: Paste the meeting link and invite the bot. Admit it when it asks to join; participants see it in the meeting.

transcript.confusionTitle: Participants privately asked about this (anonymous count)
transcript.empty: The transcript appears here once audio starts (or start the demo).

canvas.agentNode: Added by the agent (edit to take it over)

empty.timeline: Insights will appear above the moment they were triggered. Double-click anywhere to add a note.
empty.topicMap: Insights will gather into topic islands as the discussion moves on.
empty.issueMap: The issue map (questions, ideas, pros and cons) builds up as the agent follows the discussion.
empty.periphery: Calm mode: insights stay in the side trays; only urgent ones come to the centre.

summary.heading: Meeting so far
summary.empty: The agent summarizes the meeting as it goes.

glossary.empty: Terms the agent explains are collected here.

private.heading: Only you
private.hint: Explanations here are private. Nobody sees what you asked unless you share it — and even then it is anonymous.
private.backgroundPlaceholder: e.g. designer, new to machine learning
private.empty: Click “?” on any line of the transcript, press ? on your keyboard, or use “What was that?”.
private.failed: Could not explain this right now.

command.whatWasThatHint: Privately explain the last few seconds (shortcut: ?)
command.placeholder: Ask the agent to look something up…
command.dissentPlaceholder: A concern you'd rather not voice yourself — the agent raises it as its own…
command.privateHint: Show the result only to you
command.sent: Researching — the card is on the canvas.
command.notResearch: That does not look like something to research.

dissentResult.posted: The agent will raise it at the next pause, without your name.
dissentResult.rejected: The agent did not post this (it looked like a personal attack or off-topic).
dissentResult.rateLimited: Please wait a few minutes before raising another concern.

layoutHint.timeline: Hypothesis: anchoring each insight to the moment it was triggered makes it cheap to connect information to the talk.
layoutHint.topicMap: Hypothesis: stable spatial clusters by topic help the group see what is covered and what is missing.
layoutHint.issueMap: Hypothesis: an explicit map of questions, ideas, pros and cons counters circular talk and premature consensus.
layoutHint.periphery: Hypothesis: quiet edge trays minimize interruption; only urgent insights reach the centre.

consent.title: Before you start recording
consent.pointTranscribe: Meeting audio from this device is transcribed in real time.
consent.pointProviders: Audio and text are sent to the speech-recognition and AI services configured for this server.
consent.pointInform: Everyone in the meeting must know and agree that the meeting is being transcribed.
consent.pointStore: Transcripts and insights are stored on this server with the room.

audio.demoNote: This room replays a scripted meeting. Use “Demo” in the toolbar to play it again.
audio.rtmsNote: Enter the Zoom meeting ID in Settings → Room, then start the RTMS app in Zoom. Audio arrives automatically.
audio.headphones: Use headphones, otherwise your microphone also records other people's voices from your speakers.

error.meetingAudioMissing: No audio was shared. Choose the meeting tab and tick “Share tab audio” (or “Share system audio”).
error.serverRejected: The server could not start speech recognition.

audio.botInvited: The bot is joining. Admit it in the meeting.
audio.botFailed: The bot could not be sent.

hint.timeline: Insights hang above the utterance that triggered them.
hint.topicMap: Insights cluster by topic in frames that never move on their own.
hint.issueMap: IBIS map; evidence and challenges attach to ideas.
hint.periphery: Edge trays; only urgent items reach the centre.

hint.manual: Anyone can promote a card to the centre for everyone.
hint.auto: The agent also spotlights urgent insights.

hint.progressive: One plain sentence; click for detail (faster, lighter to read).
hint.full: Detail is generated and shown up front.

hint.breakpoint: Non-urgent cards wait for a pause or a change of speaker.
hint.immediate: Cards appear as soon as research starts.
hint.digest: Non-urgent cards are batched into a digest.
hint.shadow: Research baseline: cards are generated and logged but not shown.

hint.toast: A small notification links to the card.
hint.autoPan: The view moves to the new card when you are idle.

hint.question: Challenges are asked as Socratic questions (less face-threatening).
hint.statement: Challenges are stated as concise concerns.
hint.persona: Challenges are voiced as a stakeholder might ask them.

hint.fade: Unpinned cards fade after 5 minutes to reduce clutter.

hint.visible: Everyone sees how many people privately asked about a line (no names).
An anonymous bar shows how evenly speaking time is shared.

hint.onDemand: Sources appear only when asked for.

settings.title: Settings
settings.name: Display name
settings.locked: The room locked these options for an experiment.
settings.promotion: When several people privately ask about the same moment, post an anonymous catch-up card
settings.experimentIntro: Room-wide UX conditions. Every option embodies a hypothesis; interactions are logged on the server for comparison.

nameDialog.title: What should others call you?
nameDialog.text: Your name is shown on your cursor and on cards you request. Private questions are never linked to it.
